new.v: Money in tomato cans buried in holes in the ground (story)
new.tovw: Lead grade C: one period paper with a Marengo dateline gives the farm (both sides of the Milwaukee track north of Conroy), the hiding method, the unsolved 1898 murder and a 1904 night dig; no recovery reported.
new.n: Ole Olson's money in tomato cans, abandoned farmhouse north of Conroy
new.pl: Ole Olson's land lay on both sides of the Milwaukee track north of Conroy, Iowa Co; the house stood a little west of the track among trees he planted; exact section not yet found (ring 3 km around Conroy)
new.st: Ole Olson, an early settler who lived alone north of Conroy, distrusted banks and kept most of his money in tomato cans hidden in holes in the ground. About 1896 three masked men burned his feet until he gave up one hiding place. In September 1898 he was beaten to death; the murder was never solved and the house stood empty afterward. In late May 1904 two men drove in at night and were seen digging; four fresh holes were found around a tree near the house. Nothing is reported found. Pin is Conroy, not the farm.
new.t: Private farmland: ask first. Look for the old house site west of the former Milwaukee grade north of Conroy; a plat of 1886-1900 should name Olson's quarter. The 1904 diggers found nothing that was reported.
new.warn: Private farmland; the house is gone.
src: Evening Times-Republican (Marshalltown), 3 Jun 1904, p. 3, 'Old Crime Recalled' (Marengo dispatch; Newspapers.com 352065811)
pinev: Conroy point from the 1930 plat card; Olson's land was north of Conroy on both sides of the Milwaukee track (Evening Times-Republican, 3 Jun 1904); section not yet found
